title: Delegated Invocation Safety and Result Sanitization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we expand multi-tool chaining and function-calling support for streaming responses and structured outputs, we need robust defenses against unsafe result injection, runaway recursion, and incompatible tool contracts that can break downstream parsers or leak sensitive data.

Goal: Implement a light-weight, runtime-safe delegated-invocation layer that: (1) validates tool result shapes against declared structured-output schemas, (2) performs configurable sanitization/stripping of unsafe fields before injection into the LLM context, (3) enforces recursion/loop guards (max depth, idempotency checks, invocation budgets), and (4) integrates with our compatibility layer so older SDK clients and hosted endpoints degrade gracefully.

Scope: Server-side runtime + API contract changes; no user-facing console UI in this ticket. Prototype should include: schema validator library (JSON Schema v7 compatible), result sanitizer plugin points, recursion budget enforcement, telemetry hooks. Compatibility adapters must support current function-calling contract and our structured-output envelope.

Design decisions made so far: we will use declarative schemas attached to tool registrations (stored in model catalog metadata) rather than ad-hoc per-request validators. Sanitization will be policy-driven (allowlist/denylist and redact rules) with default safe presets for hosted customers. Recursion guard = combination of per-request invocation depth (default 6) and a budget token bucket (default 20 invocations per minute per request origin). For compatibility, if a client does not provide a schema, we apply loose-mode sanitizer and emit compatibility-warning telemetry rather than failing the request.

Constraints and non-goals: This ticket will not implement RBAC controls for tool invocation (separate work). It will not change console rollout policies. Heavy-weight schema inference for third-party tools is out of scope (we only accept explicit schemas or stable builtin parsers).

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime validates tool outputs against declared schema and rejects/flags non-conforming outputs before injection into model context.
- Sanitization policy can remove or redact fields matching configured patterns and runs in streaming mode without blocking token emission.
- Recursion/loop guard prevents runaway loops in 95% of synthetic fuzz tests and returns a clear structured error to the caller.
- Backwards compatibility: requests from pre-schema clients succeed with compatibility warning and no silent data leaks.
- Unit + integration tests and a prototype end-to-end demo with a chained 3-tool pipeline covering streaming + result injection.

Notes and rationale: We prioritize developer ergonomics (clear errors + guidance) over aggressive hard-failures for unknown clients to avoid breaking existing customers. Telemetry will include counts of sanitization actions, schema violations, recursion aborts, and per-tool invocation budgets to inform defaults tuning.

acceptance_criteria: Schema validation rejects non-conforming tool outputs with structured error (error.code: TOOL_SCHEMA_MISMATCH)
Sanitizer can redact headers/patterns and runs in streaming mode (<5ms per sanitize call at p50)
Recursion guard aborts after configured depth and emits invocation budget telemetry
Compatibility mode accepts pre-schema clients and emits compatibility_warning telemetry instead of hard-failure

comments: 2026-02-21 - Spike results: JSON Schema v7 implementation (ajv) added ~3.2ms p50 validation for 1-2kb payloads in a Node runtime. Native Rust validator (schemars/valico alternatives) explored - performance comparable; opted to prototype Rust validator for Dedicated runtime path.

2026-02-24 - Design review (pm+security): PM requests clearer error messaging for end-users; Security asked for default denylist of 'authorization','credentials','private_key' fields and explicit opt-in to return them in safe environments.
2026-02-28 - Decision: default recursion depth = 6, budget token bucket = 20 invocations per minute per request origin. These are configurable via per-project policy in dedicated/private deployments.

2026-03-02 - Prototype PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248 (runtime: schema validator + sanitizer hooks). Opened SDK adapter PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/512. Asking @helen.cho and @security-team for review.

2026-03-04 - Code review feedback: add structured telemetry fields for 'sanitize.reason' and 'schema.mismatch.path'; minor naming nits. Also add a streaming-safe sanitizer path to avoid buffering tokens for long outputs. Assigned to Marco to address.

2026-03-05 - Blocker discovered: existing KV-cache prefix injection code assumes arbitrary tool payloads and will inject raw strings into prompt builder; need to update prompt builder to accept sanitized structured tokens.
